title: Development token shortcut bypassed JWT enforcement outside production
reproduction: With AUTH_REQUIRE_JWT=true and ENVIRONMENT=development, unauthenticated POST /api/auth/token user_id=1 returned a token (HTTP 200).
fix: Reject whenever JWT enforcement is enabled, as well as in production. Explicit non-JWT local development remains available.

title: Raw forwarded headers controlled rate-limit and audit identities
reproduction: 21 login-limit requests with different raw X-Forwarded-For values avoided the 20/minute limit; the raw value also replaced the audit peer IP.
fix: Use ASGI request.client for both controls. The offline loopback API disables proxy-header normalization; shared deployments still require qualified trusted-proxy stripping and address handling. Historical audit rows are unchanged.

classification: Publisher-confirmed affected dependency; application RCE not executed
title: Installed Next 16.2.9 matches the Windows RCE advisory
fix: No upgrade authorized. Local frontend launch paths now bind 127.0.0.1; this reduces network exposure but does not patch the vulnerability.

title: Shared-beta browser/deployment policy remains unqualified
details: Observed frontend responses have no X-Frame-Options, CSP or X-Content-Type-Options. HTTPS, trusted reverse-proxy configuration, complete CSP/Cesium compatibility and clickjacking qualification remain unverified. No header architecture was changed without an exploit/compatibility assessment.
